name: Alex Haecker
bio_raw:
Alex Haecker, AIA, NCARB

alex@awharchitects.com

Alex Haecker has over 25 years of professional experience in design, architecture, historic preservation, adaptive reuse and rehabilitation. Alex has worked on a wide array of projects during the course of his career, but has focused on adaptive reuse, historic preservation, urban infill, and workplace environments. Along with his architecture practice he is deeply committed to serving the community by both serving on nonprofit boards and being a past 3 term Commissioner on the Minneapolis Heritage Preservation Commission. This dedication, both professionally and personally, affords him the extensive knowledge of historic renovations, additions, and renovations of existing buildings and spaces. His work encompasses residential, municipal, nonprofit, educational and corporate clients across the nation.

name: Nardos Shitta
bio_raw:
John Greene, AIA Associate

John has over 12 years of professional experience in design, digital fabrication, architecture, historic preservation, adaptive reuse and rehabilitation. Before entering the profession, John completed a two-year apprenticeship with a master carpenter in mid-coast Maine after a long period of moving around the country in pursuit of good snowboarding. He relishes the opportunity to collaborate with construction professionals to find innovative solutions. In addition to his professional work John teaches an undergraduate conceptual drawing course in the College of Design at the University of Minnesota. John is inspired by architectural processes that synthesize the needs of the community, create joy in the built environment, and respect the individuality of how each person occupies space.

name: Wes Pfeifer
bio_raw:
Wes Pfeifer, AIA, LEED AP

Wes brings over 25 years of architectural experience across a wide range of project types, both nationally and internationally. His work has primarily focused on multi-family housing in its many formsâincluding affordable housing, market-rate apartments, condominiums, and senior living communities.

A strong advocate for environmentally responsible design, Wes is committed to creating architecture that responds to both the needs of clients and the communities they serve. He brings deep expertise in project documentation and a thorough understanding of building and energy codes, which he uses to develop thoughtful, code-compliant solutions. His approach emphasizes integration with the surrounding context and prioritizes the experience of the end user.

name: Namdi Alexander
bio_raw:
Namdi Alexander, AIA Associate

Namdi has over 11 years of architecture and design experience. During that time, he has worked as a passionate advocate for sustainable design and construction practices within various market sectors. He finds the unique challenges of historic rehabilitation and adaptive-reuse projects rewarding, as they breathe new life into existing structures. Namdi is also committed to improving access to design professionals in our communities by spearheading outreach and engagement efforts, and volunteering as a design mentor for high-school students. In addition to his role as a mentor, Namdi serves as an adjunct instructor at the University of Minnesota, where he teaches and develops  the curriculum for Undergraduate Design Studios. 

Namdi believes empathy is essential to the design process and that thoughtful design can improve lives. As a designer, he is committed to collaborating with clients to find innovative and responsible design solutions that align with their project objectives, while contributing to the betterment of the world around us.

name: Jacob Dommer

Jacob Dommer, AIA Associate, Phius Alliance

Jacob brings an interdisciplinary skill set and a passion for sustainable design to the AWH team. With 9 years of professional experience in custom metal fabrication, art installation, project management, and architecture, he has an intuitive understanding of design rooted in collaboration, community engagement, and construction. At the University of Minnesotaâs architecture program, Jacob has hosted sustainable design charrettes, community engagement workshops, and recently led an interdisciplinary team of designers to win 2nd place in the Solar Decathlon â a net zero design competition hosted by the Department of Energy.

Now, on his way to becoming a certified passive house designer, Jacob is eager to incorporate environmental impact tools and emerging materials to design low carbon, high performing buildings that are healthy and built to last.

name: Lawrence Black

In addition, he has experience in construction administration, being an Ownerâs Representative, and running his own business,  so youâll likely find him working in all areas of AWH to streamline and improve our processes.

name: Erika Spande
bio_raw:
Erika Spande

Erika is trained in both residential and landscape design having worked in the two fields for over 10 years at design\/build and construction companies prior to joining AWH. Her designs focus on function and practicality with the use of sustainable materials and approaches both inside and out. She is also trained as a Master Water Steward and brings that expertise and knowledge to our work especially as it relates to site design, native plantings and stormwater. This blended experience of water, plants, and intimate design provides her with the insight and judgement for design solutions that are good for the people and the planet. Erika is also a key component in keeping AWH running smoothly, by managing the bookkeeping and human resources.
